content.text:
I've submitted **index 15** (Mn 0.507 / Y 0.493) as the best composition. It gave the highest photocurrent of the three I measured, **5.8×10⁻⁷ A**.

| Index | Mn fraction | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 14 | 0.658 | −9×10⁻⁸ (effectively zero) |
| 15 | 0.507 | **5.8×10⁻⁷** |
| 12 | 0.447 | 5.1×10⁻⁷ |

- **Why I started at Mn ≈ 0.66:** the models favoured YMn₂O₅ there. The machine-learned potential (MACE) put it on the stability hull, and the band-gap model (MEGNet) gave a 2.78 eV gap, low enough to absorb the 3.22 eV light. The measurement at index 14 still came out at zero.
- **Why I moved to Mn ≈ 0.5:** that is the YMnO₃ composition. MACE puts YMnO₃ on the hull and MEGNet gives it a 1.29 eV gap. Both measurements in that region produced real photocurrent.
- **The Mn-rich end (Mn > 0.7) is unmeasured.** I skipped it because YMn₃O₆ comes out slightly unstable and nearly metallic (0.36 eV gap), and the nearest measured point on that side (index 14) gave zero.
- **The Y-rich end (Mn below about 0.42) is also unmeasured.** Photocurrent dropped only a little from index 15 to index 12, so the best composition could lie on that side. The budget ran out before I could check.
- **I used none of the 5 XRD measurements,** so the phases at these compositions are predicted, not confirmed.
